Commentary.Commentary: We are back for South Africa's reply! The Bangladeshi players are in a huddle and, Najmul Hossain Shanto is giving them a last-minute pep talk. Now, they spread out to take their respective field positions. Aiden Markram and Tony de Zorzi are the openers for South Africa. Hasan Mahmud to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

With a massive advantage, the Proteas will now look to capitalize with the bat. With the pitch showing signs of turn, things could become tricky for batting in the fourth innings, so South Africa will aim to bat big and bat just once. Bangladesh, on the other hand, will have to shake off this poor batting performance and come back stronger with the ball if they hope to stay in the contest. An exciting second inning is just around the corner, stay tuned!

After winning the toss and opting to bat, nothing went right for Bangladesh. The Proteas' pacers started strong, striking early and never letting any batter settle. Wiaan Mulder set the tone with an excellent opening spell, and Kagiso Rabada soon joined in to dismantle the top order, reducing the hosts to rubble. Keshav Maharaj kept things tight from one end and, once in rhythm, worked in tandem with Dane Piedt to clean up the lower middle order. Mahmudul Hasan Joy was the only batter to cross the 20-run mark, showing some grit before falling to Maharaj. Rabada returned to the attack late and, along with Maharaj, wrapped up the innings with clinical precision. It was a well-rounded performance from the bowlers, with Mulder, Rabada, and Maharaj each claiming three wickets, while Piedt chipped in with one.

That wraps up Bangladesh's innings, and few would have expected it to end this quickly given the nature of the surface which seemed perfect for batting. This was far from a challenging pitch to bat on, but a disastrous batting display from the hosts, combined with disciplined bowling from South Africa, has seen Bangladesh bundled out for just 106 runs in their first innings.

For Bangladesh, Mehidy Hasan looked composed and confident after arriving at the crease, but his dismissal just before Lunch has only deepened the trouble for the hosts. With Mahmudul Hasan Joy still standing firm, Bangladesh will be hoping he can anchor the innings and drag them to at least 150 runs. Their focus now shifts to survival and recovery, while South Africa will look to maintain their stranglehold and wrap things up quickly. An exciting afternoon session awaits and play will resume at 6.40 am GMT, so be sure to join us for more thrilling action then!

Kagiso Rabada set the tone with a tight opening over, and it didn’t take long for Wiaan Mulder to make an immediate impact, dismissing Shadman Islam for a duck in just his first over. Mulder continued to bowl with precision and was rewarded with two more key wickets, Mominul Haque and the prized scalp of Najmul Hossain Shanto, leaving Bangladesh in disarray. Rabada soon joined the party, removing the experienced Mushfiqur Rahim, followed by Litton Das, to pin the hosts further down and achieve his feat of 300 wickets in Tests. Keshav Maharaj maintained a stranglehold from one end, building pressure relentlessly, while the pacers wreaked havoc from the other. Their persistence paid off just before the stroke of Lunch, as Maharaj picked up a crucial wicket to leave the hosts teetering at 60/6!

After winning the toss and opting to bat, the hosts struggled to weather the fiery spells from South Africa’s pacers and are now left reeling under immense pressure.

Commentary.Commentary: With all the pre-match formalities complete, we are ready for the action to begin! The two umpires make their way to the middle, and the Proteas break from a final huddle, spreading out across the field to take their positions. Shadman Islam and Mahmudul Hasan Joy stride out as the Bangladesh openers, determined to get their side off to a solid start. Kagiso Rabada has the new ball in hand and looks fired up, ready to set the tone for South Africa. Away we go!
The match officials and the captains of both teams lead their players out to the middle for the national anthems. South Africa's anthem will play first, followed by the Bangladesh anthem!

Aiden Markram, the skipper of South Africa says they would have wanted to bat first as well but now will make sure they try to extract whatever is on offer early on and then bring in spin. Adds that the preparation has been good over the last few days and the team is in good headspace and excited for the games. Mentions that Matthew Breetzke makes his debut and plays this game and they are going with two spinners.

Najmul Hossain Shanto, the skipper of Bangladesh says that they will bat first. Adds that the wicket looks dry and batting in 4th innings will be harder. Adds that it can happen in cricket, losing a series but they played excellent cricket against Pakistan. Mentions that the preparation has been really good and they have some key players who are eager to do well in this game.

PITCH REPORT - Ed Rainsford is down in the middle for the pitch analysis. He says the surface is hard with a nice grass covering on it. Adds that the weather is hazy but the surface looks very hard and the teams winning the toss would love to bat and post big total on the board.

Shukri Conrad, the Head Coach of South Africa is also down for a quick chat. He says the preps have been good and they expect this to be spin dominated. Adds that once they came in, they thought the conditions were tough but they are now confident and have covered all the bases. Mentions that the batters are slightly inexperienced but that is a challenge they look forward to. States that they have the right balance and the best of spinners in Keshav Maharaj.

Phil Simmons, the Head Coach for Bangladesh is down for a chat. He says that they got 3 days of good practice and they are ready for the game. Adds that the key is that they need to back their strengths and need to exploit the home conditions well. Says that it will spin on this wicket.

On the other hand, South Africa will also be without their regular skipper Temba Bavuma, with Aiden Markram stepping in to lead the side. The Proteas’ top order has struggled with consistency lately and will be looking to find their rhythm in this series. However, what could truly set South Africa apart is their lethal bowling attack. Kagiso Rabada will spearhead the pace department, while Keshav Maharaj will take charge of the spin, which is likely to play a key role on this surface. With crucial World Test Championship points on the line, South Africa will push hard for a positive result, but Bangladesh at home presents a formidable challenge. All signs point to a thrilling encounter ahead, and the toss is just moments away!

After a disappointing series loss to India, Bangladesh will be eager to turn their fortunes around at home and put up a strong challenge against the Proteas. The absence of Shakib Al Hasan in this opening Test is a significant blow, especially with the all-rounder set to retire after this series. However, the hosts boast enough depth and talent to take the fight to South Africa. Najmul Hossain Shanto will need to lead from the front, but the batting unit, struggling for consistency in recent times must step up collectively if Bangladesh hope to make a strong impact.
